title: Language in the Flow of Time: Time-Series-Paired Texts Weaved into a Unified Temporal Narrative
abstract: While many advances in time series models focus exclusively on numerical data, research on multimodal time series, particularly those involving contextual textual information, remains in its infancy. With recent progress in large language models and time series learning, we revisit the integration of paired texts with time series through the Platonic Representation Hypothesis, which posits that representations of different modalities converge to shared spaces. In this context, we identify that time-series-paired texts may naturally exhibit periodic properties that closely mirror those of the original time series. Building on this insight, we propose a novel framework, Texts as Time Series (TaTS), which considers the time-series-paired texts to be auxiliary variables of the time series. TaTS can be plugged into any existing numerical-only time series models and effectively enable them to handle time series data with paired texts. Through extensive experiments on both multimodal time series forecasting and imputation tasks across benchmark datasets with various existing time series models, we demonstrate that TaTS can enhance multimodal predictive performance without modifying model architectures.
problem: Integrating paired texts with time series remains underdeveloped despite advances in LLMs and time series learning, particularly when capturing periodic properties shared between text and numerical data.
approach: Texts as Time Series (TaTS) treats time-series-paired texts as auxiliary variables, enabling any numerical-only time series model to handle multimodal data by leveraging periodic properties shared between modalities.
contribution: TaTS enhances multimodal predictive performance on forecasting and imputation tasks without modifying model architectures across various benchmark datasets.
